info.name: Server Moderation Session Service
info.description:
Team 16 - "Student ID, please". Server Moderation Session Service, owner Postoronca Dumitru.

Every request name carries the status code it expects, so the collection can be checked mechanically. Folders marked 'run in order' capture ids into collection variables and depend on the requests before them - use the Collection Runner on the folder rather than firing individual requests.

Order: health -> auth -> caller identity -> sessions (contract) -> events - decision.recorded -> ending the shift -> errors - setup -> error codes -> sessions (beyond contract) -> dev - task timeout -> cleanup.

Every request goes through the Gateway. Requests that act for a player send `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`; the 'auth' folder registers four fresh players through Player Service (POST /player/players), logs them in and stores their ids and tokens, so run it first. Fresh players keep the run independent of the seed - the seeded dima_mod, maxim_jr and vlad_jr are members of the seeded active session, the contract's own example - and of the other collections; the cleanup folder deletes them. The Gateway validates the token and forwards only `X-Player-Id`. Service-only routes (POST /events, /dev/*, /health/ready) send `X-Service-Token: {{service_token}}`, which must equal SERVICE_TOKEN in the CPR .env.

Set `base_url` if the Gateway is not on http://localhost:8080. The player ids are captured at registration.

Full reference: docs/SERVER_MODERATION_SESSION_SERVICE.md in the Common Public Repository.

caller identity
item.description:
Proves how this service decides which player a request acts for, without creating anything: each request either fails authentication outright, or gets past it to a Player Service lookup that 404s. Safe to run at any point.

The primary mechanism is `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` with the player id in the `sub` claim, unverified - matching University Record Service. `X-Player-Id` is kept as a fallback because a bare UUID is easier to type into curl than a JWT.

request.description: 401 rather than 400: the request is well formed, it simply says nothing about who is making it - which is the status a real token check would return too.

item.name: a token that is not a JWT -> 401 UNAUTHENTICATED (Gateway)

request.description: A token present but unusable is refused rather than falling through to the fallback header: silently masking a bad token with a stale id would make the failure impossible to diagnose.
Only the Bearer scheme is accepted (case-insensitively, per RFC 7235).

item.name: events - decision.recorded, as Moderation Service pushes it (contract)
item.description: Until POST /api/v1/events exists, nothing delivers decision.recorded from Moderation Service. This endpoint accepts the exact envelope Moderation's relay will push and runs it through the same handler POST /api/v1/events will call. It is mounted only when ENABLE_DEV_ENDPOINTS is true, and it moves a session's score with no credential - so it is off outside a demo.

request.description: A correct decision adds SCORE_PER_CORRECT * difficulty to the score, increments applications_processed, and marks the current applicant decided so the Moderator may ask for the next one.

item.name: 2. POST the SAME event again -> 200 duplicate:true

request.description: The contract requires every consumer to dedupe by event_id, because an event may be delivered more than once. A replay is a success, not an error - and the 'duplicate' flag is how a caller can see the deduplication fire. Run request 1 and this one, then check the session: the counters must have moved once.

exec: pm.test('200 - a replay is a success', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.description: Ending the shift freezes the per-player result and writes session.ended. request.description: A malformed id is a client bug. Reporting it as 404 would hide that behind a legitimate-looking answer.

The contract says a player's request carries their JWT and the endpoint takes player_id from it. No token issuer exists yet, so the id arrives in the X-Player-Id header. This is a stand-in for the JWT's sub claim, not authentication.

request.description: Run the 'errors - setup' folder first: junior_a is in the pair lobby it opens. A player in a lobby or an active session cannot open another. Run the 'errors - setup' request first to get a fresh lobby. Only the creator may start a session.
The solo lobby from the setup folder. A shift needs a Moderator and at least one Junior Moderator.
